record.original_question: Let K be a compact subset of R^2 that meets every residue class modulo Z^2, and let A = (K-K) intersect Z^2. Which finite generating sets of Z^2 can arise in this way? In particular, can one realize the axis-cross set {(0,0),(±1,0),(0,±1)}?

evidence.quote: For n = 2, which sets of generators arise in this fashion? Specifically, is there a K (compact and hitting every residue class modulo 1) such that A ⊆ {(x, y)colonxy = 0}? Even more specifically, is there a K with A = {(0, 0),(±1, 0),(0, ±1)}?
Note since the end of the conference: Renling Jin has solved this problem. Independently, and by different methods, Mario Szegedy has obtained a partial solution.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a compact set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ a 2-dimensional $\mathcal{N}$-set if for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^2$ there exists $y \in K$ with $y - x \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ (equivalently, $K$ meets every residue class modulo $\mathbb{Z}^2$). For such a $K$, define
$$A(K) := (K - K) \cap \mathbb{Z}^2 = \{a - b : a, b \in K\} \cap \mathbb{Z}^2.$$
It is known that $A(K)$ is always a finite generating set of the group $\mathbb{Z}^2$.

Question: Characterize which finite symmetric subsets $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^2$ containing $0$ and generating $\mathbb{Z}^2$ can be realized as $A = A(K)$ for some 2-dimensional $\mathcal{N}$-set $K$. In particular:

(a) Does there exist a 2-dimensional $\mathcal{N}$-set $K$ such that $A(K) \subseteq \{(x,y) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 : xy = 0\}$ (i.e. all integer differences lie on the union of the two coordinate axes)?

(b) More specifically, does there exist a 2-dimensional $\mathcal{N}$-set $K$ with
$$A(K) = \{(0,0),\, (\pm 1, 0),\, (0, \pm 1)\}?$$
artifact.category_tag: Difference sets and tilings of Euclidean space
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that Renling Jin resolved the problem (with an independent partial solution by Mario Szegedy). Jin's work on 2-dimensional 𝒩-sets shows that any such set must contain distinct points whose integer difference is not purely along a single coordinate axis, ruling out the axis-cross realization.

status_evidence.snippet: Research in nonstandard analysis, additive-combinatorial number theory, set theory.
status_evidence.claim: Renling Jin works on additive combinatorics and difference sets, consistent with his having solved the 2-dimensional 𝒩-set generator problem.

status_evidence.title: Renling Jin's research works
status_evidence.snippet: Every two-dimensional 𝒩-set A must contain distinct points x,y such that x-y is in Z^2 and x-y is not purely along one axis.
status_evidence.claim: Jin proved that the axis-cross generating set cannot be realized, resolving the specific question.
